metadata.process_title: Wood Pyrolysis to Bio Oil & Biochar
metadata.process_description:
This example analyzes a wood biomass pyrolysis process. Pyrolysis is a treatment at increased temperatures in a non-oxidizing environment, which converts the organic raw material into solid char, liquid bio-oil, and gases.
Pyrolysis processes can in principle convert renewable wood biomass, agricultural residues, and even post-use rubbers and plastics, into readily usable forms of energy, and feedstock for production of advanced fuels and chemicals. Gasification of bio-oil followed by Fischer-Tropsch and catalytic synthesis processes can lead to production of many basic chemicals and fuels which have the potential replace the existing fossil-based production.
This pyrolysis plant processes 30 MT/h of wood biomass with a moisture content of around 45% w/w. The plant is assumed to be operative for 8400 hours (350 days) per year
